reason: No proposal has measured results. Rank the NEON transpose first because it tests a distinct conversion method on the already measured TB path; the poor TB scores do not show that transpose caused the regression. TA is valid but adds a timed B transpose while retaining generated B packing and adding A packing. The four-step unroll is distinct from the measured two-step version, though that version gives no evidence that further unrolling will help. Scratch repacking changes traversal and resembles an unpromoted row-half-first experiment. The 288-byte scratch stride has no cache-geometry evidence and adds 16 KiB. The paired K-loop proposal may duplicate the measured two-step schedule unless its actual instruction order differs. Fused transpose recomputes each A element 16 times, so its stated work increase makes it the weakest proposal.
